title: A Reminder: Critique Should Help, Not Hurt
author: Natural-Spirit-3481
selftext:
Seems like half the posts are getting downvoted to 0, followed by one vague, harsh comment with no constructive feedback. Calling someone’s work “sloppy” based solely on an image doesn’t help anyone improve.

This should be a place where we support each other, share advice, and help people grow, not judge or tear others down. If there’s something that can be improved, explain why and offer helpful feedback instead of just criticizing.

You guys need to do better.

comments.author: CertainBlue
comments.body:
Eh, I feel like the problem of this sub is that a lot of people post half-baked, derivative ideas like "look at this x game clone I made in 1 prompt" over and over again, without any kind of creativity or thought put into them. Which is fine, but not worth sharing, you're just toying with the model. WE know- it's powerful, we know it can do these things, you don't need to prove it for the 100th time. These kind of posts aren't even worth a carefully crafted reply because it's a waste of everyone's time.  
I'd much prefer if people focused on exploring novel concepts, refined projects that have had months of work put into them, with posts that actually sell you on why their game is worthwhile, worth checking out.

comments.author: Baraga91
comments.body:
In the past 10 hours, 5 posts were made that sit at 0 upvotes, with many many more within that timeframe sitting comfortably in the positive numbers...

Just because we embrace AI in game dev doesn't mean we should be glazing every single post claiming to "do what AAA games did not so long ago!" or "take the next step in [genre]!" or other clickbait, while a lot of them clearly kust threw a couple prompts into an AI without much thought, process or result.

You want people to take us more serious? Set the bar high enough to be taken serious.

replies.author: Baraga91
replies.body:
If you post spammy questions or stupid answers in r/AskHistorians, the mods will come down on you like a ton of bricks. It's incredibly strict, but it's the sub with the best quality content, consistency and reputation out there.

The lesson is that you have to maintain a standard people can hold you to, and as long as we're going to tolerate (and, if OP gets their way, encourage) truly sloppy content, we'll be hurting our own cause.

comments.author: Verdux_Xudrev
comments.body:
The down-voting could be brigading, but I want to address your "Critique Should Help, Not Hurt[](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/?f=flair_name%3A%22Discussion%22)" part with a few words.

What someone might say about your game might hurt you, but it might help the game in the long run. I'm not saying that folks can't be mean and that all advice you get is gold, but it's up to the dev to do better. AI is tool to make things easier, not an excuse to show off trash and expect to be praised. If you're just wanting to show off what AI can do raw, that's fine. But if it this a serious project, you need to treat it like it.

replies.author: PhilosophyforOne
replies.body:
It’ not that I disagree with you about the first part, and silence is definitely a better option than a scathing criticism. 

But I still find myself agreeing with OP. We’re becoming a very gate-keeperish society, if our immediate reaction is to tell someone what they did is shit/slop (even when it objectively is.)

Maybe part of the problem is AI glazing the user. Or maybe it’s just that when you’re suddenly for the first time able to make any type of game at all, it’s a pretty amazing experience and you might lose some of the ability to critique your own work/you’re just really proud of having made something, because on your own scale it’s still good (even if on the general scale it’s slop).

For all of that though.. I do think OP’s post reminded me to be kinder to people here, atleast. It doesnt mean praising their work, and you’re not obligated to take out a bunch of your time to give really directed, personalized feedback. But maybe even just pointing out more politely that: ”Hey! A lot of the content here looks sort of generic AI-style work. I think this might need a fair bit of effort. Sorry to bear the bad news here, and good luck!”, is still better than just.. attacking it. 

That said. Silence is not the worst thing either. There shouldnt be a strong obligation, but it is a shame if we stsrt being too critical, since the genuine slop and people’s earnest effort might easily get mixed up.

comments.body: Agree with this.  If you dont like something.. either skip it entirely, or give constructive feedback, not negative.  This is basic adulting and human courtesy.  If you say "AI slop" you sound like a person who just wants to be nasty to other people online.

comments.author: god-damn-the-usa
comments.body: Yes, calling someones image slop does help. Because if customers see your game and think it looks like slop, they are going to click away immediately. Just because it hurts your feelings doesn't mean its wrong or unhelpful. Critique isn't to make you feel good, and it often hurts even when constructive.
